reading.body:
The Franklin campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity across 80,000 square feet, enough to run roughly 150 GPU-dense racks at 40 kW each or 600 enterprise racks at 10 kW each, depending on actual tenant workloads and power allocation choices the operator has not disclosed.

At 6 MW, this facility would be entirely consumed by a single large AI training cluster. That scale places it well below hyperscale data center benchmarks but sufficient to support substantial compute workloads if the operator has sized the building for that purpose. The operator's own facility page does not specify how power density is allocated or whether this building is currently oriented toward AI, general colocation, or regulated workloads.

The certification stack, SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITRUST, and ISO 27001, qualifies the facility for financial services and healthcare tenants. These are compliance prerequisites, not indicators of current use or performance. They mean the facility can house regulated workloads, not that it does.

Among 24 Tennessee facilities tracked here, only this one publishes IT capacity, so the state total of 6 MW reflects a single site, not the state's actual installed base. The ranking represents a data gap, not evidence of scale. Tennessee's data center footprint beyond this facility remains unquantified on published operator pages.
